title: Book Two · Chapter 23: Jun Takes the Other Chair
story:
On Tuesday, Miss Wu reads out the pairs.

Ronan waits beside his bag. Leo stands by the window with a pencil in his hand.

“Ronan and Jun,” Miss Wu says.

Ronan turns his head. Jun is already moving a chair.

Leo will work with the child beside the window. Mei has another partner. She puts her own book page under her exercise book for later.

Jun carries his pencil tin to Ronan's desk.

“Which side?” he asks.

Ronan moves his bag off the empty chair. “This one.”

Miss Wu gives each pair a story. Ronan and Jun have two copies of the same page. There is a bowl at the top of it. Below the picture are these words:

A woman lends her big bowl to a girl. The girl carries it home. The girl's mum puts soup in the bowl. They eat lunch.

After lunch, the girl returns the bowl to the woman. The woman washes it at her own home. Then she puts three apples in the bowl. She gives one apple to the girl.

The girl carries that apple home. Her mum smiles. Now the girl and her mum can eat an apple too.

Ronan reaches the bottom first. Jun still has two lines to read.

“I am done,” Ronan says.

Jun puts one finger beside his line. He keeps reading.

Ronan watches the pencil on Leo's table. It is moving across a card already. He looks back at Jun.

“Are you nearly done?”

“Yes. Let me finish.”

Ronan waits. He taps his ruler once, then stops. He knows that sound from the child at his old desk.

Jun finishes and looks up.

“Shall we take half each?” Ronan asks.

“All right. You can start. I can finish.”

Jun points to the bowl picture. “But we need the whole story too.”

“I read the whole story.”

“I mean both of us. I need your part too.”

Miss Wu comes past. They show her the line between their two parts.

“Read both parts first,” she says. “Then choose your notes together.”

Jun takes out his three-box card from yesterday. Ronan has his exercise book. Its spaces are much bigger.

“Your card is too small,” Ronan says.

“It is for notes. The story is here.”

Jun touches the page. He wants room on the desk for both copies. Ronan puts his book a little further back.

They write GIRL and WOMAN in the first box. Then Jun adds MUM.

“Three people,” he says.

“Three apples too,” Ronan says.

“Do not put the apples in the people box.”

Ronan draws three tiny heads. One head looks like an apple. Jun adds a short line for its neck. Both boys laugh quietly.

They finish only the first box today. There is other work before lunch. Jun wants his chair back at his own desk for the number lesson.

Ronan helps him carry it. The chair catches against Ronan's bag. They stop and move the bag first.

At the end of school, Jun puts his story copy inside his book. Ronan folds his own copy once and puts it in his bag.

“Tomorrow,” Jun says.

“We can finish quickly,” Ronan answers.

Jun looks at the two empty boxes on the card. He puts it away with his copy.
studyGuide:
## 重点表达

- lends＝借给
- copy＝同一页的一份
- nearly＝快要、几乎
- neck＝脖子

## 理解问题

1. 碗属于谁？女孩在什么时候把碗送回去？
2. Jun为什么坚持两个人都要读完整个故事？

## 从认词到读句子

正文原句：*Jun puts one finger beside his line.*

**Jun / puts one finger / beside his line.**

Jun／把一根手指放下／放在正在读的那一行旁。beside说明位置。
